title: Residue-field rank criterion for maps of finite free modules
statement: Let $R$ be a ring, let $u:R^{\oplus m}\to R^{\oplus n}$ be a homomorphism of finite free $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-free-module, def-weil-pbc-projective-module], and let $\mathfrak p$ be a prime ideal. If $u\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is injective, then there is $f\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $u_f$ is injective and $\operatorname{Coker}(u_f)$ is finite free over $R_f$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. If $u\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is an isomorphism, then there is $f\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $u_f$ is an isomorphism.

split_report.summary: Checked the finite-free specialization of Stacks Tag 00O0. The proof is the finite matrix minor argument: an injective residue-field map has a nonvanishing maximal minor, whose determinant becomes a unit after principal localization and yields an identity block and finite-free cokernel; in the equal-rank isomorphism case the determinant itself becomes a unit and the adjugate gives the inverse. No smaller independent lemma was introduced because these are the item’s own elementary matrix steps.
